question:
A 62-year-old male presents with a 5-month history of watery diarrhea accompanied by episodic
crampy abdominal pain. He reports a 1.8-kg weight loss over 6 months despite maintaining normal
appetite, and his wife notes facial and neck flushing that occurs after meals or during distress. His
medical history includes asthma diagnosed one year ago and hypertension. He takes albuterol inhaler
and enalapril, and consumes one beer daily. Physical examination reveals a temperature of 36.7°C,
pulse of 75/min, and blood pressure of 159/93 mm Hg. Cardiac examination shows a grade 2/6 systolic
murmur at the left sternal border and fourth intercostal space. The abdomen is mildly tender without
guarding or rebound. Lungs are clear on auscultation. Complete blood count is normal. If left untreated,
which of the following conditions poses the greatest risk to this patient? Answer Choices: (A)
Malabsorption syndrome (B) T-cell lymphoma (C) Achlorhydria (D) Metastatic liver disease (E)
Right-sided heart failure (F) Dementia (G) Carcinoid heart disease (H) Bronchial carcinoid (I)
Megaloblastic anemia (J) Cushing syndrome
 A. Metastatic liver disease
B. Dementia
C. Carcinoid heart disease
D. Achlorhydria
E. Right-sided heart failure
F. Cushing syndrome
G. Bronchial carcinoid
H. T-cell lymphoma
I. Malabsorption syndrome
J. Megaloblastic anemia
